t: You're looking at the W. T. Stead Memorial, a Grade II listed bronze bas-relief on the Victoria Embankment. It sits on a block beside Temple Pier, near the King's Reach Memorial. It remembers William Thomas Stead, an English newspaper editor and pioneer of investigative journalism. At the Pall Mall Gazette he ran influential campaigns, including his 1885 series The Maiden Tribute of Modern Babylon, which backed the bill that raised the age of consent from thirteen to sixteen. The sculptor was Sir George Frampton, who also made the Edith Cavell Memorial and the Peter Pan statue.
